description:
The issue mutation arms reload what they changed through `storage` and print hand-built payloads. This moves them to library handlers that report the entity the executor mutation returns.

## Background

In `crates/jit/src/main.rs`, `IssueCommands::{Create, Update, Delete, Assign, Claim, Unassign, Reject, Release, ClaimNext, BatchCreate}` call the executor and then `storage.resolve_issue_id` and `storage.load_issue` to report the result; `create` also lists every issue through `storage` to evaluate graph rules. `delete` builds its success body with `json!` and its confirmation failure with an inline `JsonError`; `update` substitutes `GenericError` for unclassified failures under `--json`; `batch-create` prints its dry-run outcome and its `{key: id}` result as bare serialized documents outside the success envelope; `issue delete` and `issue batch-create` fall back to `CommandResponse` in the schema. The executor mutations now return the updated `Issue`.

A handler in `crates/jit/src/dispatch/` takes its parsed arguments and a `CommandContext` (the executor and the `OutputMode { json, quiet }`) and returns `anyhow::Result<Outcome<R>>`; one registration per group generates the group's dispatch and its schema response lookup. Success responses are types defined in the output module (`crates/jit/src/output/`) or output constructors wrapping a command-layer result, each deriving `JsonSchema` and a human rendering; list payloads are `ListEnvelope<K, T, E>` instantiations; failures are returned as errors that `jit::output::failure::classify` maps to one code and exit status; a non-zero findings result is `Outcome`'s findings variant, rendered under `--json` as the failure envelope with the report in `error.details` and its registered code as the exit status.

On main, `run()` in `crates/jit/src/main.rs` parses the arguments and calls `dispatch()` in `main.rs`, which holds the command match; the arms and inline code this issue places in `run()` live in `dispatch()`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `run()` dispatches `issue create|update|delete|assign|claim|unassign|reject|release|claim-next|batch-create` to handlers in `crates/jit/src/dispatch/issue.rs`, and `main.rs` keeps no arm body for them.
- [hard] REQ-02: These handlers make no `storage` call: each reports the `Issue` (or the batch result) its executor mutation returns.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each leaf returns its registered response type and the schema names it; the `batch-create` dry run and real run print through the one success emitter, and a test states their new payload form.
- [hard] REQ-04: The handlers return failures as errors with no substituted code, inline `JsonError` or `std::process::exit`; a test asserts that an `issue update` failure the classifier maps to a specific code reports that code on both paths instead of `GENERIC_ERROR`.
- [hard] REQ-05: Where a leaf's exit codes change, its rows in `CommandSchema::generate_command_exit_codes` (`crates/jit/src/schema.rs`) state the new codes and `docs/reference/exit-codes.md` is regenerated.
- [hard] REQ-06: Human output, success payloads and exit codes of these leaves are otherwise unchanged, and the existing suites pass without weakened assertions.

## Decisions

- D-01: REQ-06's unchanged human output and payloads exclude the warnings of the lifecycle, delete and update leaves, which follow the uniform warnings rule (as for 20fc3b92 D-01 and 1ac651c7 D-02): `issue update --filter` rule warnings print as `Warning: <short>: <msg>` lines on stderr instead of a stdout block, `update` warnings are suppressed under `-q`, and these warnings reach the `--json` envelope's shared `warnings` instead of the payload's own `(issue, message)` tuples. Those tuples are attributed messages, not structured findings, so the shared string form with the issue's short id in the text is consistent; structured findings such as check-links' `link_warnings` (file, link, kind) keep their own field (steward ruling, 2026-11-04).

## Notes

2d10f1dd makes update and reject single atomic mutations; 16d63038 changes id resolution.

Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`; inventories with function and arm citations: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/investigation.md`.
title: Issue write commands move to library handlers
